questions.question: What precondition does binary search require?
options: The array must contain unique values
The array size must be a power of 2
The array must be stored in a linked list
questions.explanation: Binary search discards half the range based on ordering.

questions.question: What is the worst-case time complexity of binary search on n elements?
questions.explanation: Each comparison halves the search range.

questions.question: What is the worst-case time complexity of linear search on n elements?
questions.explanation: It may need to check every element.

questions.question: What is the worst-case time complexity of bubble sort?
questions.explanation: Up to n passes, each with up to n comparisons.

questions.question: Why does a recursive function need a base case?
options: To stop recursion and avoid infinite calls
questions.explanation: Without a base case, calls never terminate and the stack overflows.

questions.question: What does Big-O notation describe?
options: The exact running time in seconds
An asymptotic upper bound on growth rate
questions.explanation: Big-O bounds how a function grows from above as input size increases.

questions.question: Which sorting algorithm repeatedly selects the minimum of the unsorted part and moves it into place?
questions.explanation: Selection sort swaps the minimum of the remaining elements into the next position.

questions.question: What characterizes a greedy algorithm?
options: It always stores subproblem results in a table
It makes the locally optimal choice at each step
It splits the problem into halves
questions.explanation: Greedy algorithms commit to the best immediate choice.

questions.question: What is the worst-case time complexity of merge sort?
questions.explanation: It always splits into halves (log n levels) and merges in O(n) per level.

questions.question: What is the worst-case time complexity of quick sort?
questions.explanation: Consistently bad pivots produce unbalanced partitions of size n-1.

questions.question: Which of these sorting algorithms is stable?
questions.explanation: Merge sort preserves the relative order of equal keys when merging.

questions.question: Which data structure does depth-first search use, explicitly or via recursion?
questions.explanation: DFS explores the most recently discovered vertex first.

questions.question: Dijkstra's shortest-path algorithm requires that edge weights are:
questions.explanation: A negative edge could improve an already-finalized distance.

questions.question: Which two properties make a problem suitable for dynamic programming?
questions.explanation: DP reuses solutions of repeated subproblems that compose into an optimal solution.

questions.question: What is the time complexity of the naive recursive Fibonacci fib(n) = fib(n-1) + fib(n-2)?
questions.explanation: Each call branches twice and subproblems are recomputed.

questions.question: What does T(n) = 2T(n/2) + n solve to?
questions.explanation: By the Master theorem, f(n) = Θ(n^(log2 2)) gives Θ(n log n).

questions.question: What is the worst-case lower bound for any comparison-based sorting algorithm?
questions.explanation: A decision tree must have n! leaves, so its height is Ω(n log n).

questions.question: What is the time complexity of Kruskal's MST algorithm with sorting and Union-Find?
questions.explanation: Sorting edges dominates; Union-Find operations are nearly constant.

questions.question: Which is true of the Bellman-Ford algorithm?
options: It runs in O(E log V) and needs non-negative weights
It runs in O(VE) and can detect negative-weight cycles
questions.explanation: An extra relaxation pass that still improves a distance reveals a negative cycle.

questions.question: The standard DP for 0/1 knapsack with n items and capacity W runs in O(nW). Why is it called pseudo-polynomial?
options: Its running time is polynomial in the numeric value W, not in the number of bits of W
It is polynomial only when n is small
questions.explanation: W can be exponential in its input length, so O(nW) is not truly polynomial.

questions.question: A topological ordering of a directed graph exists if and only if the graph:
options: Has no directed cycles (is a DAG)
Has a vertex with no outgoing edges
questions.explanation: A cycle would require a vertex to come before itself.

questions.question: What does T(n) = T(n-1) + n with T(1) = 1 solve to?
questions.explanation: Unrolling gives 1 + 2 + ... + n = n(n+1)/2.
